articles.text: ÀOĚRSĒN: Zhèige dìfang shi bu shi wǒmen yào qù cānguānde?
MS. OLSEN: Is this one of the places we're going to visit?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Shì. Guò liǎngtiān wǒmen jiù qù.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Yes. We'll be going in a couple of days.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Wǒ kàn, zhèige rénmín gōngshè hǎoxiàng yǒu yìdiǎnr tèbié ma, tāmende shēngchǎn zhǔyào shi shūcài hé shuǐguǒ.
MS. OLSEN: It looks to me as if this people's commune is rather special. Their production is mainly vegetables and fruits.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Nǐ shuōde yìdiǎnr yě bú cuò, zhèi jiù shi yǒu míngde Sìjìqīng Rénmín Gōngshè.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: You're absolutely right. This is the famous Sìjìqīng People's Commune.
ÀOĚRSĒN: "Sìjìqīng"?
MS. OLSEN: "Sìjìqīng?"
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Duì le, "yìnián sìjì"de "sìjì," "qīng shān lǜ shuǐ"de "qīng." Nín zài Běijīng Fàndiàn chīde cài dàbùfen dōu shi tāmen shēngchǎnde.

CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Yes. "Sìjì" ("four seasons") as in "yìnián sìjì" ("throughout the four seasons of the year"), and "qīng" ("green") as in "qīng shān lǜ shuǐ" ("green hills and green water"). Most of the food you eat at the Běijīng Hotel is produced by them.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Ou!
MS. OLSEN: Oh!
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Tāmen gōngshè yǒu sìwànduō mǔ tǔdì, dàbùfen dōu shi càidì.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Their commune has over forty thousand mǔ of land. Most of it is vegetable plots.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Càidìde miànjī zhàn bǎifēnzhī duōshao? Zhèr yǒu méiyou xiězhe?
MS. OLSEN: What percentage do the vegetable plots take up? Is it written here?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Zhèr xiězhe ne. Càidì zhàn liǎngwàn liǎngqiān mǔ, yíbànr duō yìdiǎnr.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Yes, it is. The vegetable plots take up 22,000 mǔ, a little more than half.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Nàme, hái yǒu yíwàn bāqiān mǔ ne? Zhòngde dōu shi shénme?
MS. OLSEN: And what about the other 18,000 mǔ? What do they grow there?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Tāmen shuō yòng yíwàn mǔ dì zhòng liángshi.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: They say they use 10,000 mǔ to plant grain.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Ng. Zhǔyào shēngchǎn shénme liángshi?
MS. OLSEN: Mm. What grain do they mainly produce?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Dàozi, yǒu míngde Jīngxīdào! Nín lái zhèr yǐhòu, tiāntiān chī!
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Rice, the famous Capital-West rice. You've been eating it every day since you came here.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Ā! Yuánlái "Jīngxīdào" shi Sìjìqīng shēngchǎnde. Tīngshuō chǎnliàng hěn gāo ou! Mǔchǎn yǒu yìqiānduō jīn ba?
MS. OLSEN: Ah! So Sìjìqīng produces Capital-West rice. I hear that the yield is very high! The per-mǔ yield is over one thousand catties, isn't it?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Yǒu, mǔchǎn zǒng zài yìqiān yìqiān yìbǎi jīn zuǒyòu.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Yes. The per-mǔ yield is always approximately 1,100 catties.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Ng, zhēnde bú cuò. Nà lìngwài bāqiān mǔ dōu shi shuǐguǒ?
MS. OLSEN: Mm, that's really quite good. So then are the remaining 8,000 mǔ all fruits?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Shì. Tāmen gōngshède shuǐguǒ chǎnliàng yě hěn gāo.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Yes. Their commune has a very high fruit yield, too.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Wǒ hái yǒu yíge wèntí, quán gōngshè yǒu duōshao rénkǒu, yǒu duōshao láodònglì?
MS. OLSEN: I have one more question. What's the population of the whole commune, and how many laborers are there?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Yǒu yíwàn líng bābǎiduō hù, sìwàn sānqiānduō kǒu rén, liǎngwàn liǎngqiānduō láodònglì, píngjūn měige láodònglì děi guǎn liǎngmǔ dì na!
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: There are 10,800 households, over 43,000 people, and over 22,000 laborers. On the average, every laborer has to take care of two mǔ of land!
ÀOĚRSĒN: Yíge rén guǎn liǎngmǔ dì hěn xīnkǔ ma?
MS. OLSEN: Is it very hard work for one person to take care of two mǔ?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Zhòng cài, shōu cài, xiànzài hái méi bànfǎ kào jīqì, quán děi kào shǒu, zěnme bù xīnkǔ ne?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: At present they still don't have the means to adopt machines. Planting and harvesting have to be done entirely by hand. It's hard work all right.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Nǐ kàn, túpiànshang yǒu bù shǎo tuōlājī, tāmende jīxièhuà shuǐpíng xiāngdāng gāo ma.
MS. OLSEN: But look, in these pictures there are lots of tractors. Their level of mechanization is pretty high!
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Zhèige gōngshè xiāngdāng xiānjìn, yǒu yìbǎi bāshí liàng qìchē, dà xiǎo tuōlājī sānbǎi qīshiduō tái, kěshi zhèixiē qìchē zhǔyàode gōngzuò shi bǎ cài sòng dào chénglǐ qu.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: This commune is quite advanced. They have 180 automobiles, and over 370 tractors. But the main job of these vehicles is to take the vegetables into the city.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Ng, wǒ dǒng le, wǒ juéde zhèige gōngshè hěn yǒu tèdiǎn, nǐ zài duō tántan, hǎo bu hǎo?
MS. OLSEN: Mm, I see. This seems to be a very distinctive commune. Could you tell me more about it?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Hǎo a! Zhèige gōngshède měige shēngchǎn dàduì dōu yǒu zìjǐde shēngchǎn zhòngdiǎn — shēngchǎn dàduì nǐ dǒng bu dǒng?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Sure! Every production brigade of the commune has its own production priority — do you understand "production brigade"?
ÀOĚRSĒN: Wǒ zhīdao shēngchǎn dàduì, shēngchǎnduì, shénmede.
MS. OLSEN: I know about production brigades, production teams, and so forth.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Nà hǎo, wǒmen guǎn tāmen zhèizhǒng zǔzhī shēngchǎnde bànfǎ jiào zhuānyèhuà shēngchǎn.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Okay, well we call this method of organizing production of theirs specialized production.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Ā! Měige shēngchǎn dàduì dōu yǒu zìjǐde zhuānyè. Hǎojíle. Zhèi duì fāzhǎn shēngchǎn yídìng yǒu hěn dàde hǎochu.
MS. OLSEN: Ah! Each production brigade has its own specialty. Great. This must be of great help in expanding production.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Shì ma! Shēngchǎn fāzhǎnle, rénmínde shēnghuó shuǐpíng cái néng tígāo ma!
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Sure! The people's standard of living can only be raised when production expands.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Nàme, zhèizhǒng zhuānyèhuà shēngchǎn zài quánguó shi bu shi hěn pǔbiàn ne?
MS. OLSEN: So is this kind of specialized production very common throughout the whole country?
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Bú shi, quánguó dàbùfen gōngshè zhǔyào háishi shēngchǎn liángshi, zài dà chéngshìde jìn jiāoqū cái yǒu xiàng Sìjìqīng zhèiyàngrde gōngshè.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: No, most of the communes in the country still mainly produce grain. It's only in the close suburbs of big cities that one finds communes like Sìjìqīng.

ÀOĚRSĒN: Yǒu jīhui, wǒ hái xiǎng qù cānguān yìliǎngge pǔtōngde gōngshè. Hái yǒu píngyuán hé shāndìde nóngyè shēngchǎn qíngkuàng dàgài yě yǒu hěn duō bù tóng, rúguǒ yǒu jīhui, wǒ hěn xiǎng qù liǎojiě yíxià tāmende qūbié.

MS. OLSEN: If I get the chance, I'd also like to visit one or two ordinary communes. Also, farming production is probably very different on the plains from that in mountainous regions. If it's possible, I'd like very much to go look into the differences.
CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: Hǎode. Zuìjìn jǐnián Zhōngguó nóngyè jiànshè fāzhǎnde hěn kuài. Nín shi zhuānjiā, nínde yìjiàn duì wǒmende gōngzuò yídìng yǒu hěn dàde bāngzhù, wǒ yídìng duō gěi nín ānpái jǐge dìfang.

CHÉN GUÓQIÁNG: All right. In the past few years, China's agricultural construction has been moving rapidly ahead. As an expert, your opinions can help us a great deal in our work. I'll be sure to arrange a few more visits for you.
ÀOĚRSĒN: Bú bì kèqi, nín ānpáihǎole, qǐng zǎo yìdiǎnr gàosu wo.
MS. OLSEN: You needn't be polite. Please let me know soon after you've made the arrangements.
